title.zh: 卷22 列傳第14 周惠達 馮景 楊寬 兄穆 儉 柳慶 子機
title.en: Volume 22 Biographies 14: Zhou Huida; Feng Jing; Yang Kuan; elder brothers Mu and Jian; Liu Qing; Zi Ji
title.raw: 卷22 列傳第14 周惠達 馮景 楊寬 兄穆 儉 柳慶 子機 Volume 22 Biographies 14: Zhou Huida; Feng Jing; Yang Kuan; elder brothers Mu and Jian; Liu Qing; Zi Ji

sentences.zh: 周惠達 馮景 楊寬 兄穆 儉 柳慶 子機

translations.literal: Zhou Huida; Feng Jing; Yang Kuan; elder brothers Mu and Jian; Liu Qing; Zi Ji
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida; Feng Jing; Yang Kuan; Yang Mu and Yang Jian (elder brothers); Liu Qing; Zi Ji (Liu Ji)

sentences.zh: 周惠達字懷文，章武文安人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Huida, styled Huaiwen, was a man of Wen'an in Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida, styled Huaiwen, came from Wen'an in Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 父信，少仕州郡，歷樂鄉、平舒、平成三縣令，皆以廉能稱。

translations.literal: His father Xin, in youth served in prefecture and commandery, and successively was magistrate of Lexiang, Pingshu, and Pingcheng—the three posts all won praise for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin entered service young in local government and served successively as magistrate of Lexiang, Pingshu, and Pingcheng, earning a reputation for integrity and competence in all three posts.

sentences.zh: 惠達幼有志操，好讀書，美容貌，進退可觀，見者莫不重之。

translations.literal: From youth Huida had ambition and integrity, loved reading, had fine appearance, and comportment in advance and retreat was estimable—those who saw him all held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Zhou Huida had strong character and ambition, loved books, was handsome, and carried himself with such grace that everyone who met him respected him.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王蕭寶夤為瀛州刺史，召惠達及河間馮景同在閤中，甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi of Wei Xiao Baoyin was governor of Ying Province, he summoned Huida and Feng Jing of Hejian to serve together in his secretariat, and treated them with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi of Wei, became governor of Ying Province, he summoned Zhou Huida and Feng Jing of Hejian to join his staff and treated them with great honor.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤還朝，惠達隨入洛陽。

translations.literal: When Baoyin returned to court, Huida followed him into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin returned to the capital, Huida went with him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 領軍元义勢傾海內，惠達嘗因寶夤與义言論，釜歎重之，於座遺惠達衣物。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Guard Yuan Yi's power tilted all within the seas; Huida once, through Baoyin, discoursed with Yi—Yi sighed and held him in esteem, and at the gathering sent Huida garments.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Guard Yuan Yi dominated the realm; Zhou Huida once spoke with him through Baoyin, and Yi sighed in admiration and sent him clothing from his seat.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，魏臨淮王彧北討，以惠達為府長流參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Prince of Linhuai of Wei Yuan Ye marched north in punitive expedition and appointed Huida recorder of his headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiaochang era, Prince of Linhuai Yuan Ye marched north on campaign and made Zhou Huida recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 及万俟醜奴等構亂，蕭寶夤西征，惠達復隨入關。

translations.literal: When Wanqi Chounu and others stirred rebellion, Xiao Baoyin marched west in expedition and Huida again followed into the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanqi Chounu and others raised rebellion, Xiao Baoyin marched west and Zhou Huida followed him through the passes again.

sentences.zh: 寶夤後與賊戰不利，退還，仍除雍州刺史，令惠達使洛陽。

translations.literal: Later Baoyin fought the rebels unsuccessfully, withdrew, and was nevertheless appointed governor of Yong Province, sending Huida as envoy to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin was defeated by the rebels and withdrew, he was nonetheless appointed governor of Yong Province and sent Zhou Huida as envoy to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 未還，而寶夤反謀聞于京師。

translations.literal: Before he returned, Baoyin's plot to rebel became known in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before Huida could return, word of Baoyin's planned rebellion reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 有司以惠達是其行人，將執之。

translations.literal: The authorities, because Huida was his envoy, were about to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities intended to arrest him because he had been Baoyin's envoy.

sentences.zh: 乃私馳還，至潼關，遇大使楊侃。

translations.literal: He therefore secretly galloped back; at Tong Pass he met the grand envoy Yang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He fled back in secret and at Tong Pass met the imperial envoy Yang Kan.

sentences.zh: 侃謂惠達曰：「蕭氏逆謀已成，何為故入獸口？

translations.literal: Kan said to Huida: "The house of Xiao's treasonous plot is already formed—why deliberately enter the beast's maw?
translations.idiomatic: Kan said to Huida: "The Xiao clan's treason is already set—why ride straight into the tiger's mouth?

sentences.zh: 」惠達曰：「蕭王為左右所誤，今往，庶其改圖。

translations.literal: " Huida said: "Prince Xiao has been misled by those around him—if I go now, perhaps he may change his design.
translations.idiomatic: " Huida replied: "Prince Xiao has been led astray by his advisers. If I go now, he may yet change course.

sentences.zh: 」及至，寶夤反形已露，不可彌縫，遂用惠達為光祿勳、中書舍人。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, Baoyin's rebellion was already exposed and could not be patched over; Huida was therefore appointed Superintendent of Bright Luxuriance and Attendant within the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " When he arrived, Baoyin's rebellion was already plain and could not be concealed; Baoyin then appointed Huida Superintendent of Bright Luxuriance and Attendant within the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 寶夤旣敗，人悉逃散，唯惠達等數人從之。

translations.literal: Once Baoyin was defeated, people all fled and scattered; only Huida and a few others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was defeated, everyone fled; only Zhou Huida and a handful of others stayed with him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤語惠達曰：「人生富貴，左右咸言盡節，及遭厄難，乃知歲寒也。」

translations.literal: Baoyin said to Huida: "In life one enjoys wealth and honor, and those at one's side all speak of utmost loyalty—but only when one meets adversity does one know the cold of winter."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin said to Huida: "In prosperity those around you all swear undying loyalty—but only in hardship do you learn who stands firm in the cold of winter."

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳獲寶夤送洛，留惠達為府祭酒，給其衣馬，卽與參議。

translations.literal: Heluo Yue captured Baoyin and sent him to Luoyang; he kept Huida as libationer on his staff, supplied him with clothing and horses, and immediately consulted with him on policy.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Yue captured Baoyin and sent him to Luoyang; he kept Zhou Huida as libationer on his staff, gave him clothes and horses, and at once brought him into council.

sentences.zh: 岳為關中大行臺，以惠達為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Yue was Grand Commissioner's Office for Guanzhong, he appointed Huida gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue became Grand Commissioner for Guanzhong, he appointed Zhou Huida gentleman-attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗使至洛，魏孝武與惠達語及世難。

translations.literal: Once sent to Luoyang, Emperor Xiaowu of Wei conversed with Huida about the woes of the age.
translations.idiomatic: On one mission to Luoyang, Emperor Xiaowu of Wei spoke with Zhou Huida about the troubles of the times.

sentences.zh: 惠達陳天下事勢，述岳有誠節，唯以憂國定亂為事。

translations.literal: Huida laid out the situation under Heaven, described Yue's loyalty and integrity, and how he took only worry for the state and settling turmoil as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida set out the state of the realm, praised Yue's loyalty, and said that Yue cared for nothing but securing the country and ending the chaos.

sentences.zh: 言辭激切，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: His words were fierce and pointed; the Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His speech was forceful and urgent; the Emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 及還，具以白岳。

translations.literal: When he returned, he fully reported this to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he told Yue everything.

sentences.zh: 岳曰：「人生於天，受命於君，豈有利人榮祿，而不憂其禍難？

translations.literal: Yue said: "One is born under Heaven and receives mandate from one's lord—how can one seek others' glory and stipend yet not worry over their calamities and hardships?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "We are born under Heaven and owe our lives to our lord—how can we enjoy rank and salary from another and not share his peril?

sentences.zh: 卿之所奏，實獲吾心。

translations.literal: What you reported truly reaches my heart.
translations.idiomatic: What you said is exactly what I feel.

sentences.zh: 」自是更被親禮。

translations.literal: " From then on he was still more treated with intimacy and honor.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on Yue treated him with even greater intimacy and respect.

sentences.zh: 岳每征討，恒命惠達居守。

translations.literal: Whenever Yue went on campaign, he always ordered Huida to remain and hold the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yue marched out, he left Zhou Huida behind to hold the base.

sentences.zh: 又轉岳府屬。

translations.literal: He was also transferred to staff member of Yue's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to a staff post in Yue's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，悅得惠達，欲官之。

translations.literal: Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue; Yue got hold of Huida and wanted to give him office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, the latter seized Zhou Huida and tried to give him a post.

sentences.zh: 惠達辭以疾，不見許，乃遁入漢陽之麥積崖。

translations.literal: Huida declined on grounds of illness; when this was not accepted he fled into the Maiji cliffs in Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida pleaded illness; when Houmochen Yue refused to accept the excuse, he fled to the Maiji cliffs in Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 悅平，惠達歸於太祖，卽用秦州司馬，安輯隴右。

translations.literal: Once Yue was pacified, Huida submitted to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, who immediately appointed him military administrator of Qin Province to pacify and settle Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue was defeated, Zhou Huida came over to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, who at once made him military administrator of Qin Province to pacify Longyou.

sentences.zh: 及太祖為大都督總管兵起雍，復以惠達為府司馬，便委任焉。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai as Grand Governor General gathered troops at Yong, he again made Huida military administrator of his headquarters and entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, as Grand Governor General, raised troops at Yong, he again made Zhou Huida headquarters military administrator and entrusted him with real authority.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武詔太祖尚馮翊長公主，以惠達為長史，赴洛陽奉迎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei ordered Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to marry the Grand Princess of Fengyi; Huida was made chief administrator and went to Luoyang to escort her in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei ordered Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to marry the Grand Princess of Fengyi; Zhou Huida was made chief administrator and went to Luoyang to escort her.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，遇孝武已西，卽令惠達先。

translations.literal: Reaching Tong Pass, they found Xiaowu had already gone west, and Huida was ordered to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass they learned that Xiaowu had already fled west, and Zhou Huida was sent on ahead.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂惠達曰：「昔周之東遷，晉鄭是依。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Huida: "Formerly when Zhou moved east, it relied on Jin and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Zhou Huida: "When the Zhou court moved east, it leaned on Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 今乘輿播越，降臨關右，吾雖猥當其任，而才愧昔人。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage is cast adrift and has descended upon Guan Right. Though I unworthily bear this charge, my talent falls short of men of old.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne is driven into exile and has come to Guan Right. I am unworthy of this burden and lack the gifts of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 卿宜戮力，共成功業，以取富貴也。

translations.literal: You should join your strength with mine to complete the enterprise and win wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: If you give me your full strength, we can finish the work and win fortune together.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「惠達宦游有年，屬明公一匡之運，富貴之事，非所敢望。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Huida has served in office for many years, and now meets your lordship's fortune in righting the realm—wealth and honor are not what I dare hope for.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "I have served in office for many years and now meet your fortune in restoring order. Wealth and rank are not what I seek.

sentences.zh: 但願明公威德加于天下，惠達得效其尺寸，則志願畢矣。」

translations.literal: I only wish your lordship's might and virtue might reach all under Heaven, and that Huida may render even a hand's breadth of service—then my ambition would be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: I only hope your power and virtue may spread across the realm, and that I may do whatever small service I can—then my wish is complete."

sentences.zh: 太祖為大將軍、大行臺，以惠達為行臺尚書、大將軍府司馬，封文安縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was made Grand General and Grand Commissioner's Office; Huida was made Commissioner of the Grand Commissioner's Office, military administrator of the Grand General's headquarters, enfeoffed Viscount of Wen'an with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was made Grand General and head of the Grand Commissioner's Office; Zhou Huida became Commissioner of that office and military administrator of the Grand General's headquarters, enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太祖出鎮華州，留惠達知後事。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai went out to garrison Hua Province and left Huida to manage affairs in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai went out to garrison Hua Province, he left Zhou Huida in charge of affairs behind him.

sentences.zh: 于時旣承喪亂，庶事多闕。

translations.literal: At that time, having inherited the chaos of disorder, the myriad affairs were mostly lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The region had just emerged from chaos, and nearly everything still needed to be built from scratch.

sentences.zh: 惠達營造戎仗，儲積食糧，簡閱士馬，以濟軍國之務，時甚賴焉。

translations.literal: Huida built military equipment, stored provisions, inspected troops and horses—to meet the needs of army and state—and the age relied heavily upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida organized arms and armor, stockpiled grain, and reviewed troops and horses to meet the needs of army and state, and the court came to depend on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 為安東將軍，拜太子少傅，進爵為伯，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the East, appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, advanced in rank to earl, fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, raised to earl, and given three hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 尋除中書令，進爵為公，增邑通前九百戶，加衛大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, advanced in rank to duke, fief totaling nine hundred households with previous grants, and added Defender Grand General and Left Grand Master of Bright Luxuriance.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Director of the Palace Secretariat, raised to duke with a total fief of nine hundred households, and given the additional titles Defender Grand General and Left Grand Master of Bright Luxuriance.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he concurrently served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he also served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 其年，太祖與魏文帝東征，惠達輔魏太子居守，總留臺事。

translations.literal: That same year, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and Emperor Wen of Wei marched east in expedition; Huida assisted the Heir Apparent of Wei in holding the rear, overseeing all matters of the capital left behind.
translations.idiomatic: That year Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and Emperor Wen of Wei marched east; Zhou Huida stayed behind to assist the Wei Heir Apparent and oversee all capital affairs.

sentences.zh: 惠達前後辭讓，帝手詔答曰：「西顧無憂，唯公是屬。

translations.literal: Huida repeatedly declined; the Emperor's handwritten edict replied: "Looking west, I have no worry—I rely on you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida tried repeatedly to decline; the Emperor answered in his own hand: "With you watching the west I need not worry—the realm rests on you alone.

sentences.zh: 蕭、寇之重，深所寄懷。

translations.literal: The weight of Xiao and Kou I deeply entrust to your care.
translations.idiomatic: The threat from Xiao and the raiders I deeply entrust to your care.

sentences.zh: 」及邙山失律，人情駭動。

translations.literal: " When at Mount Mang the army lost discipline, people's hearts were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: " When the army suffered defeat at Mount Mang, public morale collapsed in alarm.

sentences.zh: 趙青雀率東人據長安子城反，惠達奉太子出渭橋北以禦之。

translations.literal: Zhao Qingque led easterners to seize Chang'an's inner citadel in rebellion; Huida escorted the Heir Apparent north of Wei Bridge to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qingque led eastern troops in rebellion and seized the inner citadel of Chang'an; Zhou Huida escorted the Heir Apparent north of Wei Bridge to meet them.

sentences.zh: 軍還，青雀等伏誅。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Qingque and his fellows were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Qingque and his followers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Masters of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Masters of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為右僕射。

translations.literal: After some time he again served as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he again became Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 自關右草創，禮樂缺然。

translations.literal: Since Guan Right was newly established, rites and music were largely absent.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Right was still being built from nothing, and rites and music were almost wholly lacking.

sentences.zh: 惠達與禮官損益舊章，至是儀軌稍備。

translations.literal: Huida together with the rites officials revised and adapted old statutes; by then ceremonial regulations were gradually complete.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida worked with the rites officials to revise old regulations, and by then court ceremony was gradually taking shape.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝因朝奏樂，顧謂惠達曰：「此卿之功也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei, during a court audience with music playing, turned and said to Huida: "This is your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At court, as music was performed, Emperor Wen of Wei turned to Zhou Huida and said: "This is your doing.

sentences.zh: 」尋拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: " Soon he was appointed Equal in Triple Majesty to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon made Equal in Triple Majesty to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 惠達雖居顯職，性謙退，善下人，盡心勤公，進拔良士。

translations.literal: Though Huida held eminent office, by nature he was modest and retiring, good to those below him, devoted in public service, advancing and selecting worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held high office, Zhou Huida was modest by nature, treated subordinates well, served the public with full devotion, and promoted worthy men.

sentences.zh: 以此人皆敬而附之。

translations.literal: For this reason people all revered him and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: For this everyone respected him and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 十年，薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 子題嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ti succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ti succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，以惠達著績前代，追封蕭國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang under Sui, because Huida had achieved merit in the previous dynasty, he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era under Sui, Zhou Huida was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Xiao for his service to the former dynasty.

sentences.zh: 馮景字長明，少與惠達同志相友。

translations.literal: Feng Jing, styled Changming, from youth shared the same ideals with Huida and were friends.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing, styled Changming, had shared ideals with Zhou Huida from youth and they were close friends.

sentences.zh: 延

translations.literal: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Yan

translations.literal: (Jing)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Jing]

sentences.zh: 〔昌〕中，梁人寇抄徐、揚，景謂蕭寶夤曰：「今梁寇憑淩，朝廷思靖邊之將。

translations.literal: [Chang] period, Liang men raided Xu and Yang; Jing said to Xiao Baoyin: "Now Liang raiders press hard, and the court seeks a general to settle the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanxing period, Liang forces raided Xu and Yang; Feng Jing said to Xiao Baoyin: "Liang raiders are pressing hard now, and the court wants a general to secure the border.

sentences.zh: 王若能先驅效命，非唯雪家國之恥，亦是保身之長策也。

translations.literal: If you, Prince, can take the lead and offer your life in service, this is not only to wipe away the shame of state and family—it is also the long-term plan to preserve yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you take the lead and throw yourself into service, you will not only redeem the shame of your house and country—you will also save yourself.

sentences.zh: 」寶夤深然之。

translations.literal: " Baoyin deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Baoyin strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤為大都督，以景為功曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was Grand Governor General, he appointed Jing merit-court recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin became Grand Governor General, he made Feng Jing merit-court recorder.

sentences.zh: 後為右僕射，引景入省，領尚書都令史。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Vice Director and brought Jing into the secretariat, putting him in charge of the Masters of Writing chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Right Vice Director, he brought Feng Jing into the secretariat and put him in charge of the Masters of Writing chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 正光中，寶夤為關西大行臺，又假景陵江將軍，領大行臺都令史，從寶夤征討。

translations.literal: In Zhenguang, Baoyin was Grand Commissioner for Guanxi; he also provisionally made Jing General Who Crosses the River, put him in charge of the Grand Commissioner's chief clerks, and had him follow Baoyin on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era Baoyin became Grand Commissioner for Guanxi; he also made Feng Jing General Who Crosses the River in provisional appointment, chief clerk of the Grand Commissioner's Office, and took him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 寶夤將舉兵反，景固諫，不從。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was about to raise troops in rebellion, Jing firmly remonstrated, but Baoyin would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was preparing to rebel, Feng Jing argued against it firmly, but Baoyin would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗後，景還洛。

translations.literal: After Baoyin was defeated, Jing returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin's defeat, Feng Jing returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷先聞景有諫言，故免之。

translations.literal: The court had already heard that Jing had remonstrated, and therefore exempted him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already heard of Feng Jing's remonstrance, and so spared him punishment.

sentences.zh: 除奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 汝陽王元叔昭為隴右大行臺，啟景為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Prince of Ruyang Yuan Shuzhao was Grand Commissioner for Longyou and recommended Jing as gentleman-attendant of the Grand Commissioner's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shuzhao, Prince of Ruyang and Grand Commissioner for Longyou, recommended Feng Jing as gentleman-attendant on the Grand Commissioner's staff.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳為大都督，又以景為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Heluo Yue was Grand Governor General, he again made Jing gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Heluo Yue became Grand Governor General, he again made Feng Jing gentleman-attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖平侯莫陳悅，除景洛陽郡守，尋兼行臺左丞，留守原州。

translations.literal: After Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai pacified Houmochen Yue, Jing was appointed governor of Luoyang commandery; soon he also served as Left Assistant Commissioner of the Grand Commissioner's Office and remained to hold Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai defeated Houmochen Yue, Feng Jing was made governor of Luoyang commandery; he soon also served as Left Assistant Commissioner and stayed behind to hold Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，封高陽縣伯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Jing was enfeoffed Earl of Gaoyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fled west, Feng Jing was enfeoffed Earl of Gaoyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、行臺尚書，加瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Commissioner of the Grand Commissioner's Office, with Ying Province added to his charge.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant and Commissioner of the Grand Commissioner's Office, with the added post of governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 大統初，行涇州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he administered Jing Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he administered affairs in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 楊寬字景仁，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Kuan, styled Jingren, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kuan, styled Jingren, came from Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 祖恩，魏鎮遠將軍、河間內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather En was General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of the Interior of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather En was General Who Pacifies the Distance and Interior Administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 父鈞，博學強識，舉秀才，拜大理平，轉廷尉正。

translations.literal: His father Jun was broadly learned and strong in memory; he passed the provincial examination, was appointed Equalizer of the Court of Justice, and was transferred to Director of Trials.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun was learned and had a prodigious memory; he passed the provincial examination, became Equalizer of the Court of Justice, and was transferred to Director of Trials.

sentences.zh: 累遷，歷洛陽令、左中郎將

translations.literal: By cumulative promotion he served as magistrate of Luoyang, left commandant of the palace guard
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts as magistrate of Luoyang, left commandant of the palace guard

translations.literal: (jun)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: jun]

sentences.zh: 、華州大中正、河南尹、廷尉卿、安北將軍、七兵尚書、北道大行臺、恒州刺史、懷朔鎮將

translations.literal: , grand selector of Hua Province, Intendant of Henan, Director of the Court of Justice, General Who Pacifies the North, Director of the Seven Armies, Grand Commissioner of the Northern Route, governor of Heng Province, garrison commander of Huaishuo
translations.idiomatic: , grand selector of Hua Province, Intendant of Henan, Director of the Court of Justice, General Who Pacifies the North, Director of the Seven Armies, Grand Commissioner of the Northern Route, governor of Heng Province, and garrison commander of Huaishuo

translations.literal: (jun)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: jun]

sentences.zh: ，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: , and died at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: , and died at his post.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空公，追封臨貞縣伯，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary, Duke of Works, posthumously enfeoffed Earl of Linzhen, posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works, posthumously enfeoffed Earl of Linzhen with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 寬少有大志，每與諸兒童游處，必擇高大之物而坐之，見者咸異焉。

translations.literal: From youth Kuan had great ambition; whenever he played with other children, he always chose the highest seat, and those who saw this all regarded him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yang Kuan had great ambition; when he played with other children he always took the highest seat, and onlookers found it remarkable.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗解屬文，尤尚武藝。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was quite skilled in literary composition and especially valued martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he wrote competently and above all prized martial skill.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: At twenty he was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 屬鈞出鎮恒州，請從展效，乃改授將軍、高闕戍主。

translations.literal: When Jun went out to garrison Heng Province, Kuan asked to follow and prove himself; he was therefore changed in appointment to general and commandant of Gaolue Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun went out to garrison Heng Province, Yang Kuan asked to go with him and prove his worth; he was therefore reappointed general and commandant of Gaolue Pass.

sentences.zh: 時茹茹旣亂，其主阿那瑰來奔，魏帝遣使納之，詔鈞率兵衛送。

translations.literal: At that time the Ruru were already in disorder; their lord Anagui came in flight, the Wei Emperor sent envoys to receive him, and ordered Jun to lead troops to escort and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ruru were then in turmoil; their lord Anagui fled to Wei, the Wei Emperor sent envoys to receive him, and ordered Jun to lead troops to escort and protect him.

sentences.zh: 寬亦從，以功拜行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Kuan also followed; for merit he was appointed gentleman-attendant of the Grand Commissioner's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kuan went too, and for his service was made gentleman-attendant on the Grand Commissioner's staff.

sentences.zh: 時北邊賊攻圍鎮城，鈞卒，城民等推寬守禦。

translations.literal: At that time northern border rebels attacked and besieged the garrison town; Jun died, and the townspeople and others pushed Kuan to hold and defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Northern rebels then besieged the garrison town; when Jun died, the townspeople pressed Yang Kuan to take command of the defense.

sentences.zh: 尋而城陷，寬乃北走茹茹。

translations.literal: Soon the city fell; Kuan then fled north to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell, and Yang Kuan fled north to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 後討鎮賊，破之，寬始得還朝。

translations.literal: Later they campaigned against the garrison rebels, defeated them, and only then could Kuan return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Later the garrison rebels were defeated in campaign, and only then could Kuan return to court.

sentences.zh: 魏廣陽王深與寬素相委昵，深犯法得罪，寬被逮捕。

translations.literal: Prince Shen of Guangyang of Wei and Kuan had long trusted each other intimately; when Shen offended the law and was charged, Kuan was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen of Guangyang of Wei and Yang Kuan had long been close; when Shen broke the law and was charged, Kuan was arrested.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊時為侍中，與寬有舊，藏之於宅，遇赦得免。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei was attendant at the palace; having old ties with Kuan, he hid him in his residence, and Kuan was spared when an amnesty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei, then attendant at the palace, had old ties with Kuan and hid him at home; an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 除宗正丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed deputy director of the imperial clan court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 北海王顥少相器重，時為大行臺，北征葛榮，欲啟寬為左右丞，與參謀議。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai, had admired him from youth; then serving as grand field secretariat, he was campaigning north against Ge Rong and wished to nominate Kuan as left or right aide to join in strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai, had valued him since youth; then grand field secretariat on a northern campaign against Ge Rong, he wished to nominate Kuan as left or right aide for counsel in planning.

sentences.zh: 寬辭以孝莊厚恩未報，義不見利而動。

translations.literal: Kuan declined, saying Xiaozhuang's deep favor had not yet been repaid and that principle forbade moving for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan declined, saying Xiaozhuang's deep favor was still unpaid and that duty forbade acting for gain.

sentences.zh: 顥未之許。

translations.literal: Hao did not approve it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao did not agree.

sentences.zh: 顥妹婿李神軌謂顥曰：「楊寬義士也，匹夫猶不可奪志，況義士乎。

translations.literal: Hao's brother-in-law Li Shengui said to Hao: "Yang Kuan is a man of principle; even an ordinary man cannot have his resolve taken from him—how much less a principled man?
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother-in-law Li Shengui said to him: "Yang Kuan is a man of principle; even a common man's resolve cannot be forced—how much less a principled man's?

sentences.zh: 王今強之以行，亦恐不為人用。

translations.literal: If Your Highness now forces him to go, I fear he will not serve you as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: If you force him now, I fear he will not serve you willingly."

sentences.zh: 」顥乃止。

translations.literal: " Hao thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao thereupon dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 孝莊踐阼，拜通直散騎侍郎，領河南尹丞，行洛陽令。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang took the throne, Kuan was appointed irregularly-attending gentleman attendant at the scattered cavalry, concurrently supervisor of the Henan governor's office, and acting magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang acceded, Kuan was made irregularly-attending gentleman attendant at the scattered cavalry, Henan governor's supervisor, and acting magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 邢杲反，寬以都督從太宰、上黨王元天穆討平之。

translations.literal: When Xing Gao rebelled, Kuan as area commander followed the Grand Marshal, Yuan Tianmu Prince of Shangdang, and helped put down the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Gao rebelled, Kuan as area commander followed Grand Marshal Yuan Tianmu, Prince of Shangdang, and helped put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 就拜通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed irregularly-attending regular attendant at the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made irregularly-attending regular attendant at the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 師未還，屬元顥自梁入洛，孝莊出居河內。

translations.literal: The army had not yet returned when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang from Liang; Xiaozhuang withdrew to Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army returned, Yuan Hao entered Luoyang from Liang and Xiaozhuang withdrew to Henei.

sentences.zh: 天穆懼，計無所出，集諸將謀之。

translations.literal: Tianmu was afraid and could think of no plan; he gathered the generals to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu was alarmed and at a loss; he gathered the generals to counsel together.

sentences.zh: 寬曰：「吳人輕跳，非王之敵。

translations.literal: Kuan said: "Southerners are light and fickle—they are no match for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan said: "Southerners are rash and fickle—not a match for Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 況懸軍深入，師老兵疲，強弩之末，何能為也。

translations.literal: Moreover they are an army far from home and deep in enemy territory, their force aged and soldiers weary—at the end of a strong crossbow's power, what can they do?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they are an army deep in hostile country, old in the field and weary in the ranks—spent like the last force of a strong crossbow; what can they do?

sentences.zh: 願徑取成皋，會兵伊洛，戮帶定襄，於是乎在。

translations.literal: I ask that we strike straight for Chenggao, concentrate troops at the Yi and Luo, and cut off the belt and settle Xiang—that is where victory lies.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a direct strike on Chenggao, mass troops at the Yi and Luo, and cut the enemy off and settle the field—that is where victory lies.

sentences.zh: 此事易同摧朽，王何疑焉。

translations.literal: This affair is as easy as breaking rotten wood—why does Your Highness hesitate?"
translations.idiomatic: This is as easy as snapping rotten wood—why hesitate?"

sentences.zh: 」天穆然之，乃引軍趣成皋，令寬與爾朱能為後拒。

translations.literal: " Tianmu approved, thereupon led the army toward Chenggao, and ordered Kuan and Erzhu Neng to serve as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianmu agreed, led the army toward Chenggao, and ordered Kuan and Erzhu Neng to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 尋以衆議不可，乃回赴石濟。

translations.literal: Soon, because the assembled opinion was against it, he turned back toward Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, when the generals' counsel went against it, he turned back toward Shiji.

sentences.zh: 寬夜行失道，後期。

translations.literal: Kuan marched by night, lost his way, and arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan marched by night, lost the road, and arrived late.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸言：「寬少與北海周旋，今不來矣。

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Kuan has long had dealings with the Prince of Beihai—now he will not come."
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said: "Kuan has long been close to the Prince of Beihai—now he will not come."

sentences.zh: 」天穆答曰：「楊寬非輕於去就者也，其所逗留，必有他故。

translations.literal: " Tianmu replied: "Yang Kuan is not one to lightly change sides; whatever delay brings him, there must be another reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianmu replied: "Yang Kuan is not one to treat loyalty lightly; if he is delayed, there must be another reason.

sentences.zh: 吾當為諸君保明之。

translations.literal: I shall vouch for him before you all."
translations.idiomatic: I will answer for him to you all."

sentences.zh: 」語訖，候騎白寬至。

translations.literal: " When he had finished speaking, scout riders reported Kuan's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: " As he finished, scout riders reported that Kuan had arrived.

sentences.zh: 天穆撫髀而笑曰：「吾固知其必來。

translations.literal: Tianmu slapped his thigh and laughed: "I knew all along he would come."
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu slapped his thigh and laughed: "I knew he would come."

sentences.zh: 」遽出帳迎之，握其手曰：「是所望也。

translations.literal: " He immediately went out of the tent to welcome him, grasped his hand, and said: "This is what I hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: " He rushed from the tent to meet him, took his hand, and said: "This is what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 」卽給牛三十頭、車五乘、綿絹一十五車、羊五十口。

translations.literal: " He thereupon gave him thirty oxen, five carts, fifteen cartloads of cotton and silk, and fifty sheep.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave him thirty oxen, five carts, fifteen cartloads of cotton and silk, and fifty sheep.

sentences.zh: 與天穆俱謁孝莊於太行，拜散騎常侍、安東將軍。

translations.literal: Together with Tianmu he paid homage to Xiaozhuang at Taihang and was appointed regular attendant at the scattered cavalry and general who pacifies the east.
translations.idiomatic: With Tianmu he paid homage to Xiaozhuang at Taihang and was made regular attendant at the scattered cavalry and general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 仍為都督，從平河內，進圍北中。

translations.literal: He continued as area commander, followed in pacifying Henei, and advanced to besiege Beizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He remained area commander, followed in pacifying Henei, and advanced to besiege Beizhong.

sentences.zh: 時梁將陳慶之為顥兵守北門，天穆駐馬圍外，遣寬至城下說慶之。

translations.literal: At that time Liang general Chen Qingzhi was holding the north gate for Hao's forces; Tianmu halted his horse outside the siege line and sent Kuan to the foot of the wall to persuade Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Chen Qingzhi then held the north gate for Hao's army; Tianmu halted outside the siege and sent Kuan to the wall to persuade Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 寬先自稱姓名，然後與語，備陳利害，勸令早降。

translations.literal: Kuan first announced his name and only then spoke with him, fully setting forth advantage and harm and urging an early surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan first gave his name and only then spoke, setting out the stakes in full and urging an early surrender.

sentences.zh: 慶之不答。

translations.literal: Qingzhi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃曰：「賢兄撫軍在此，頗欲相見。

translations.literal: After a long while he finally said: "Your worthy brother the Army Protector is here—I should quite like to meet him."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he said: "Your worthy brother the Army Protector is here—I should like to meet him."

sentences.zh: 」寬答曰：「僕兄旣力屈

translations.literal: " Kuan replied: "My brother, having exhausted his strength before
translations.idiomatic: " Kuan replied: "My brother, having exhausted his strength before

translations.literal: (xiong)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: xiong]

sentences.zh: 〔王〕威，跡淪逆黨，人臣之理，何煩相見。

translations.literal: [Wang] authority, his tracks fallen among the rebel party—in the logic of subject and minister, why trouble with a meeting?
translations.idiomatic: Wang's might, his tracks fallen among the rebel party—as a subject, why trouble with a meeting?

sentences.zh: 向所以先申姓名者，豈不知兄在彼乎。

translations.literal: The reason I announced my name first—did you think I did not know my brother was there?
translations.idiomatic: I announced my name first—did you think I did not know my brother was there?

sentences.zh: 直以信不見疑，忠為令德耳。

translations.literal: It was simply that good faith should not be suspect, and loyalty is the highest virtue.
translations.idiomatic: It was simply that trust should not be doubted and loyalty is the highest virtue.

sentences.zh: 僕之昆季，幸不待言。

translations.literal: As for my brothers, surely there is no need to speak.
translations.idiomatic: As for my brothers, surely nothing need be said.

sentences.zh: 但當議良圖，自求多福。

translations.literal: You should only consider a good plan and seek your own blessing."
translations.idiomatic: You should only plan wisely and seek your own good fortune."

sentences.zh: 」天穆聞之，謂左右曰：「楊寬大異人，何至不惜形便如此。

translations.literal: " When Tianmu heard this, he said to those beside him: "Yang Kuan is a most unusual man—how could he go so far as to disregard his kin without shame like this!"
translations.idiomatic: " When Tianmu heard this, he told those beside him: "Yang Kuan is a remarkable man—to go so far as to set kin aside without shame!"

sentences.zh: 」自是彌敬重之。

translations.literal: " From this he respected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on he respected him all the more.

sentences.zh: 孝莊反正，拜中軍將軍、太府卿、華州大中正，封澄城縣伯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang restored order, Kuan was appointed general of the central army, grand minister of the treasury, chief arbiter of Hua Province, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chengcheng with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang restored order, Kuan was made general of the central army, grand minister of the treasury, chief arbiter of Hua, and Baron of Chengcheng with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮被誅，其從弟世隆等擁部曲燒城門，出據河橋，還逼京師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong was executed, his cousin Shilong and others mustered their troops, burned the city gates, went out and seized Heqiao, and turned back to threaten the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was executed, his cousin Shilong and others rallied their troops, burned the city gates, seized Heqiao, and turned back to threaten the capital.

sentences.zh: 進寬鎮北將軍、使持節、大都督，隨機扞禦。

translations.literal: Kuan was promoted to general who pacifies the north, bearer of the staff of authority, grand area commander, to repel the enemy as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was promoted to general who pacifies the north, bearer of the staff of authority, and grand area commander to repel the enemy as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 世隆謂寬曰：「豈忘太宰相知之深也？

translations.literal: Shilong said to Kuan: "Have you forgotten how deeply the Grand Marshal knew and favored you?"
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said to Kuan: "Have you forgotten how deeply the Grand Marshal favored you?"

sentences.zh: 」寬答曰：「太宰見愛以禮，人臣之交耳。

translations.literal: " Kuan replied: "The Grand Marshal treated me with courtesy—that was merely the exchange between subject and lord.
translations.idiomatic: " Kuan replied: "The Grand Marshal treated me with courtesy—that was only the bond between lord and subject.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，事君常節。

translations.literal: Today's affair is the constant duty of serving one's lord."
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair is the standing duty of serving one's lord."

sentences.zh: 」世隆北走，寬追至河內。

translations.literal: " Shilong fled north; Kuan pursued him to Henei.
translations.idiomatic: " Shilong fled north, and Kuan pursued him to Henei.

sentences.zh: 俄而爾朱兆陷洛陽，囚執孝莊帝。

translations.literal: Soon Erzhu Zhao captured Luoyang and imprisoned Emperor Xiaozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang and imprisoned Emperor Xiaozhuang.

sentences.zh: 寬還洛不可，遂自成皋奔梁。

translations.literal: Kuan could not return to Luoyang, so he fled from Chenggao to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to return to Luoyang, Kuan fled from Chenggao to Liang.

sentences.zh: 至建業，聞孝莊帝弒崩，寬發哀盡禮。

translations.literal: Reaching Jianye, he heard that Emperor Xiaozhuang had been assassinated; Kuan observed mourning with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianye he heard that Emperor Xiaozhuang had been assassinated and observed mourning with full rites.

sentences.zh: 梁武義之，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang admired his righteousness and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang admired his loyalty and treated him very generously.

sentences.zh: 尋而禮送還朝。

translations.literal: Soon he was courteously sent back to the north.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent back north with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 至下邳，爾朱仲遠啟復寬官爵，留為大行臺吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiapi, Erzhu Zhongyuan memorialized to restore Kuan's rank and title and kept him as director of the Masters of Writing under the grand field secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi, Erzhu Zhongyuan memorialized to restore Kuan's rank and title and kept him as director of the Masters of Writing under the grand field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，改授散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、給事黃門侍郎，監內典書事。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Kuan was reassigned as regular attendant at the scattered cavalry, general of rapid cavalry, gentleman of the yellow gate attending to affairs, and overseer of the inner palace library.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Kuan was reassigned regular attendant at the scattered cavalry, general of rapid cavalry, gentleman of the yellow gate attending to affairs, and overseer of the inner palace library.

sentences.zh: 時夏州戍兵數千人據兗州反，詔寬兼侍中，節度諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: At that time several thousand garrison troops from Xia Province seized Yan Province and rebelled; an edict appointed Kuan concurrently attendant at the palace to command the armies and put down the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand Xia Province garrison troops seized Yan and rebelled, an edict made Kuan concurrently attendant at the palace to command the armies and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 中尉綦俊與寬有宿憾，誣以他罪，劾之。

translations.literal: Chief jailer Qi Jun bore an old grudge against Kuan; he trumped up other charges and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief jailer Qi Jun bore an old grudge against Kuan, trumped up other charges, and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 孝武謂侍臣等曰：「楊寬清直，朕極知其無罪，但不能杜法官之奏耳。

translations.literal: Xiaowu said to the attendant ministers: "Yang Kuan is upright and honest—I know very well he is innocent, but I cannot block the prosecutors' memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu told the attendant ministers: "Yang Kuan is upright and honest—I know he is innocent, but I cannot block the prosecutors' memorial."

sentences.zh: 」事下廷尉，尋得申釋。

translations.literal: " The case was referred to the court of judicial review, and before long he was cleared on appeal.
translations.idiomatic: " The case went to the court of judicial review, and before long he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 又除黃門侍郎，兼武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was again appointed gentleman of the yellow gate and concurrently general of martial guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made gentleman of the yellow gate and concurrently general of martial guards.

sentences.zh: 孝武與齊神武有隙，遂召募騎勇，廣增宿衛。

translations.literal: Xiaowu had a rift with Qi Shenwu, so he recruited mounted warriors and greatly expanded the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu had a rift with Gao Huan and recruited mounted warriors, greatly expanding the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 以寬為合內大都督，專總禁旅。

translations.literal: Kuan was made grand director within the gates, with sole charge of the forbidden guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was made grand director within the palace gates, with sole charge of the forbidden guard.

sentences.zh: 從孝武入關，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He followed Xiaowu in entering the Pass region and was concurrently director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiaowu into the Pass region and was concurrently director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 錄從駕勳，進爵華山郡公，邑一千二百戶。

translations.literal: His merit in escorting the emperor was recorded; he was advanced to Duke of Huashan commandery with a fief of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in escorting the emperor was recorded, and he was raised to Duke of Huashan with a fief of twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，遷車騎大將軍、太子太傅、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry, tutor of the crown prince, and equal in rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry, tutor of the crown prince, and equal in rank to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 三年，使茹茹，迎魏文悼後。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent to the Rouran to escort back the late Empress Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was sent to the Rouran to escort back the late Empress Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 還，拜侍中、都督涇州諸軍事、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed attendant at the palace, area commander over the military affairs of Jing Province, and governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made attendant at the palace, area commander over Jing Province military affairs, and governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 五年，除驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督東雍州諸軍事、東雍州刺史，卽本州也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal in rank to the Three Dukes, area commander over the military affairs of East Yong Province, and governor of East Yong—that being his home province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal in rank to the Three Dukes, area commander over East Yong military affairs, and governor of East Yong—his home province.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉河州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to governor of He.

sentences.zh: 十六年，兼大丞相府司馬。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was concurrently grand chancellor's headquarters marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was concurrently grand chancellor's headquarters marshal.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲經略漢川，而梁宜豐侯蕭循固守南鄭。

translations.literal: Court opinion wished to advance into the Han River region, but Liang's Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xun, held Nanzheng firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The court planned to advance into the Han River region, but Liang's Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xun, held Nanzheng firmly.

sentences.zh: 十七年，寬從大將軍達奚武討之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Kuan followed Grand General Daxi Wu in campaigning against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Kuan followed Grand General Daxi Wu against him.

sentences.zh: 梁武陵王蕭紀遣將楊乾運率兵萬餘人救循，武令寬督開府王傑、賀蘭願德等邀擊之。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji, Prince of Wuling of Liang, sent General Yang Qianyun with more than ten thousand men to relieve Xun; Wu ordered Kuan to supervise opening-office holders Wang Jie, Helan Yuande, and others in intercepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji, Prince of Wuling of Liang, sent Yang Qianyun with more than ten thousand men to relieve Xun; Wu ordered Kuan to supervise opening-office holders Wang Jie, Helan Yuande, and others in intercepting them.

sentences.zh: 軍至白馬，與乾運合戰，破之，俘斬數千人。

translations.literal: The army reached Baima, joined battle with Qianyun, defeated him, and captured or killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Baima, fought Qianyun, defeated him, and captured or killed several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除南豳州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed governor of South Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was made governor of South Bin.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，入為尚書左僕射、將作大監，坐事免。

translations.literal: At the start of the deposed Emperor of Wei, he entered court as left vice director of the Masters of Writing and supervisor of palace construction, then was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the deposed Wei emperor's reign he entered court as left vice director of the Masters of Writing and supervisor of palace construction, then was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，除廷尉卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed director of the court of judicial review.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made director of the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，拜大將軍，增邑一千二百戶。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Shizong he was appointed grand general and given an additional fief of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made grand general and given twelve hundred additional households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 從賀蘭祥討吐谷渾，破之，別封宜陽縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He followed Helan Xiang in campaigning against Tuyuhun, defeated them, and was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Yiyang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Helan Xiang against Tuyuhun, defeated them, and was separately enfeoffed Duke of Yiyang county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除小冢宰，轉御正中大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed junior steward of the ancestral temple and transferred to grand master of the palace provisioners.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior steward of the ancestral temple and transferred to grand master of the palace provisioners.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，詔寬與麟趾學士參定經籍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng an edict ordered Kuan together with the Linchi academicians to collate the classical texts.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng 2 an edict ordered Kuan and the Linchi academicians to collate the classical texts.

sentences.zh: 寬性通敏，有器識。

translations.literal: Kuan was by nature penetrating and quick, with capacity and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was penetrating and quick by nature, with capacity and discernment.

sentences.zh: 頻牧數州，號為清簡。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly governed several provinces, he was known as clear and sparing.
translations.idiomatic: Having governed several provinces in succession, he was known for clarity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 曆居臺閣，有當官之譽。

translations.literal: Over long service in the central offices he had a reputation for fulfilling his post.
translations.idiomatic: Over long service in the central offices he had a reputation for doing his duty.

sentences.zh: 然與柳慶不協，欲按成其罪，時論頗以此譏之。

translations.literal: Yet he was not on good terms with Liu Qing and wished to build a case to convict him; opinion at the time quite criticized him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was at odds with Liu Qing and wished to build a case against him; opinion at the time criticized him for this.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，除總管梁興等十九州諸軍事、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he was appointed grand prefect over the military affairs of Liang, Xing, and eighteen other provinces, and governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 1 he was made grand prefect over the military affairs of Liang, Xing, and eighteen other provinces, and governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 其年，薨於州。

translations.literal: That same year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈華陝虞上潞五州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the titles of governor of the five provinces Hua, Shan, Yu, Shang, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the titles of governor of Hua, Shan, Yu, Shang, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Yuan ("Primary").

sentences.zh: 子紀嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大象末，官至上儀同大將軍、虞部下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang reign he reached upper equal-in-rank grand general and grand master of the Yu department.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang reign he reached upper equal-in-rank grand general and grand master of the Yu department.

sentences.zh: 寬二兄，穆、儉。

translations.literal: Kuan had two elder brothers, Mu and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan had two elder brothers, Mu and Jian.

sentences.zh: 穆字紹叔。

translations.literal: Mu was styled Shaoshu.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was styled Shaoshu.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，除華州別駕。

translations.literal: During Yong'an of Wei he was appointed vice director of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei Yong'an he was made vice director of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 孝武末，寬請以澄城縣伯讓穆，詔許之。

translations.literal: Near the end of Xiaowu's reign, Kuan asked to yield the barony of Chengcheng to Mu, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Xiaowu's reign, Kuan asked to yield the barony of Chengcheng to Mu, and an edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 仍拜中軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫，除車騎將軍、都督幷州諸軍事、幷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed general of the central army and grand master with the golden seal and purple tassel, then made general of chariots and cavalry, area commander over the military affairs of Bing Province, and governor of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made general of the central army and grand master with the golden seal and purple tassel, then general of chariots and cavalry, area commander over Bing military affairs, and governor of Bing.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 儉字景則。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian, styled Jingze.

sentences.zh: 偉容儀，有才行。

translations.literal: He had a fine bearing and appearance, and possessed talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in bearing and possessed both talent and character.

sentences.zh: 魏正始中，起家侍御史，加奉朝請，遷員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei he began his career as attendant censor, was additionally made court attendant, and was transferred to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era of Northern Wei he entered service as attendant censor, was additionally made court attendant, and rose to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，除鎮遠將軍、頓丘太守。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was appointed general of distant pacification and governor of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he was made general of distant pacification and governor of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 未及述職，元顥啟請隨軍。

translations.literal: Before he could take up his post, Yuan Hao requested permission for him to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume office, Yuan Hao asked that he accompany the army.

sentences.zh: 建義初，兼給事黃門侍郎、左將軍、太府少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was concurrently appointed attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, left general, and junior minister of the grand treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was concurrently made attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, left general, and junior minister of the grand treasury.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，授撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jian was appointed general who pacifies the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yang Jian was appointed general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 孝莊反正，廢於家。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was restored, Jian was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was restored to the throne, Yang Jian was dismissed and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 尋拜散騎常侍、都督潁州諸軍事、潁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed regular attendant-in-ordinary, commander of military affairs in Ying Province, and governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular attendant-in-ordinary, commander of military affairs in Ying Province, and governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 建明中，加征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Jianming he was further appointed southward general and grand master with gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianming he was further made southward general and grand master with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，除衛將軍、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, he was appointed guard general and governor of Northern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was made guard general and governor of Northern Yong.

sentences.zh: 政尚寬惠，夷夏安之。

translations.literal: His government favored leniency and kindness, and both barbarians and Chinese were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and kind, and both barbarians and Chinese lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，除侍中、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Jian was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and grand general of rapid cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Yang Jian was made attendant-in-ordinary and grand general of rapid cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大統初，以本官行東秦州事，加使持節、當州大都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, with his existing rank he acted in the affairs of Eastern Qin Province, and was additionally made bearer of the staff of authority and area commander of that province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he retained his rank while acting in Eastern Qin Province affairs, and was additionally made bearer of the staff of authority and area commander of the province.

sentences.zh: 從破齊神武于沙苑，封夏陽縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Gao Huan at Shayuan, was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiayang with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the victory over Gao Huan at Shayuan and was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiayang with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 七年，領大丞相府諮議參軍，出為都督東雍華二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he served as advisory staff member in the grand chancellor's office, then went out as commander of military affairs in Eastern Yong and Hua provinces, grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served on the advisory staff of the grand chancellor's office, then was sent out as commander of military affairs in Eastern Yong and Hua, grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Hua.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his existing offices; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his existing offices and given the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 柳慶字更興，解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Qing, styled Gengxing, was a man of Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing, styled Gengxing, came from Jie.

sentences.zh: 五世祖恭，仕後趙，為河東郡守。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Gong served Later Zhao as governor of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Gong had served Later Zhao as governor of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 後以秦、趙喪亂，乃率民南徙，居於汝、潁之間，故世仕江表。

translations.literal: Later, because Qin and Zhao fell into disorder, he led the people south in migration and settled between the Ru and Ying rivers; hence for generations they served in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qin and Zhao were torn by chaos, he led his people south and settled between the Ru and Ying rivers; the family therefore served for generations in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 祖縃，宋同州別駕，宋安郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zu was vice-prefect of Tong Province under Song and governor of Song'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zu had been vice-prefect of Tong under Song and governor of Song'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 父僧習，齊奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Sengxi was a court attendant under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengxi had been a court attendant under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏景明中，與豫州刺史裴叔業據州歸魏。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era of Wei, together with Inspector of Yu Province Pei Shuye he held the province and submitted to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era of Northern Wei he and Yu inspector Pei Shuye held the province and surrendered it to Wei.

sentences.zh: 歷北地、潁川二郡守、揚州大中正。

translations.literal: He successively served as governor of Beidi and Yingchuan commanderies and as chief rectifier of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Beidi and Yingchuan and as chief rectifier of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 慶幼聰敏，有器量。

translations.literal: From youth Qing was clever and keen, and had breadth of capacity.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Liu Qing was clever and quick-witted, with breadth of character.

sentences.zh: 博涉群書，不治章句。

translations.literal: He read widely among the classics and did not pursue textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely but did not trouble himself with textual commentary.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，閑於占對。

translations.literal: He loved wine and was skilled at impromptu reply.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and was adept at extemporaneous conversation.

sentences.zh: 年十三，因曝書，僧習謂慶曰：「汝雖聰敏，吾未經特試。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, while books were being aired in the sun, Sengxi said to Qing: "Though you are clever, I have never put you to a special test.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, while books were being aired in the sun, Sengxi said to Liu Qing: "You are clever, but I have never put you to a real test.

sentences.zh: 」乃令慶于雜賦集中取賦一篇，千有餘言，慶立讀三遍，便卽誦之，無所遺漏。

translations.literal: " He thereupon had Qing take from a miscellaneous collection of rhapsodies one rhapsody of more than a thousand words; Qing immediately read it three times and at once recited it without omitting anything.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Liu Qing take from a miscellany of rhapsodies one piece of more than a thousand words; Liu Qing read it three times on the spot and recited it from memory without a single omission.

sentences.zh: 時僧習為潁川郡，地接都畿，民多豪右。

translations.literal: At that time Sengxi was governor of Yingchuan commandery; the territory bordered the capital region, and the people included many powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sengxi was governor of Yingchuan, a district bordering the capital region where many powerful families lived.

sentences.zh: 將選鄉官，皆依倚貴勢，競來請托。

translations.literal: When he was about to select local officials, all relied on noble influence and competed in coming to request favors.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to select local officials, the powerful all leaned on noble connections and vied to solicit favors.

sentences.zh: 選用未定。

translations.literal: The selections had not yet been decided.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments had not yet been decided.

sentences.zh: 僧習謂諸子曰：「權貴請托，吾並不用。

translations.literal: Sengxi said to his sons: "Requests from the powerful—I use none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi told his sons: "I will accept none of the powerful families' requests.

sentences.zh: 其使欲還，皆須有答。

translations.literal: When their envoys wish to return, each must have a reply.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys wish to return, each must receive an answer.

sentences.zh: 汝等各以意為吾作書也。

translations.literal: Each of you, as you think fit, draft letters for me."
translations.idiomatic: Each of you draft a reply as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 」慶乃具書草云：「下官受委大邦，選吏之日，有能者進，不肖者退。

translations.literal: " Qing thereupon fully drafted a letter saying: "Your humble servant has been entrusted with a great commandery; on the day of selecting officials, the capable are promoted and the unworthy are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing then drafted a letter saying: "Your humble servant has been entrusted with a great commandery; on the day of selecting officials, the capable advance and the unworthy withdraw.

sentences.zh: 此乃朝廷恒典。

translations.literal: This is the constant rule of the court."
translations.idiomatic: This is the standing rule of the court."

sentences.zh: 」僧習讀書，歎曰：「此兒有意氣，丈夫理當如是。

translations.literal: " Sengxi read the letter and sighed: "This boy has spirit; a man ought to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: " Sengxi read it and sighed: "This boy has backbone—a man ought to be like this."

sentences.zh: 」卽依慶所草以報。

translations.literal: " He immediately replied according to Qing's draft.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied at once using Liu Qing's draft.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing began his career as court attendant.

sentences.zh: 慶出後第四叔，及遭父憂，議者不許為服重。

translations.literal: Qing had been adopted out to a fourth uncle; when he suffered his father's bereavement, critics did not permit him to wear the heavier mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing had been adopted out to a fourth uncle; when his adoptive father died, critics held that he should not wear the severest mourning.

sentences.zh: 慶泣而言曰：「禮者蓋緣人情，若於出後之家，更有苴斬之服，可奪此從彼。

translations.literal: Qing wept and said: "Rites arise from human feeling; if in the house to which one has been given out there is again coarse hemp and severest mourning, one may abandon this for that.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing wept and said: "Rites grow from human feeling; if the household that adopted me requires coarse hemp and severest mourning, one might abandon this grief for that.

sentences.zh: 今四叔薨背已久，情事不追。

translations.literal: Now my fourth uncle has long since died; the feelings of the matter cannot be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: But my fourth uncle died long ago; that bond cannot be revived.

sentences.zh: 豈容奪禮，乖違天性！

translations.literal: How can one cast aside the rites and violate natural feeling!"
translations.idiomatic: How can I cast aside the rites and violate my nature!"

sentences.zh: 」時論不能抑，遂以苫塊終喪。

translations.literal: " Contemporary opinion could not restrain him, and he therefore completed the mourning on a straw mat.
translations.idiomatic: " Public opinion could not prevail against him, and he completed the full mourning on a straw mat.

sentences.zh: 旣葬，乃與諸兄負土成墳。

translations.literal: After the burial he together with his elder brothers carried earth and completed the mound.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he and his elder brothers carried earth and built the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除中堅將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed stalwart general.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made stalwart general.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武將西遷，除慶散騎侍郎，馳傳入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to move west, Qing was appointed attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and entered the passes by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to move west, Liu Qing was made attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and rode post-haste through the passes.

sentences.zh: 慶至高平見太祖，共論時事。

translations.literal: Qing reached Gaoping and met Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; together they discussed affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing reached Gaoping and met Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; together they discussed the situation.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽請奉迎輿駕，仍命慶先還復命。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai thereupon asked to welcome the imperial carriage, and still ordered Qing to return first and report back.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai thereupon proposed to welcome the emperor, and ordered Liu Qing to return first with his reply.

sentences.zh: 時賀拔勝在荊州，帝屏左右謂慶曰：「高歡已屯河北，關中兵旣未至，朕欲往荊州，卿意何如？

translations.literal: At that time He Ba Sheng was in Jing Province; the Emperor dismissed those around him and said to Qing: "Gao Huan has already encamped north of the Yellow River, and the Guanzhong troops have not yet arrived; I wish to go to Jing Province—what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time He Ba Sheng was in Jing Province; the emperor dismissed his attendants and asked Liu Qing: "Gao Huan has already encamped north of the Yellow River, and the Guanzhong troops have not yet arrived; I wish to go to Jing Province—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」慶對曰：「關中金城千里，天下之強國也。

translations.literal: " Qing replied: "Within the passes the golden ramparts stretch a thousand li—it is the strongest state under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing replied: "Within the passes the golden ramparts stretch a thousand li—it is the strongest realm under heaven.

sentences.zh: 宇文泰忠誠奮發，朝廷之良臣也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai is loyal and earnest in exertion—a fine minister of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai is loyal and resolute—a fine minister of the court.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之聖明，仗宇文泰之力用，進可以東向而制群雄，退可以閉關而固天府。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely clarity, relying on Yuwen Tai's strength and use, advancing one can face east and control the competing lords; retreating one can close the passes and secure the heavenly storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's sagacity and Yuwen Tai's strength, advancing you can face east and master the rival lords; retreating you can close the passes and secure the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 此萬全之計也。

translations.literal: This is a plan of complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: That is the plan of complete safety.

sentences.zh: 荊州地非要害，衆又寡弱，外迫梁寇，內拒歡黨，斯乃危亡是懼，寧足以固鴻基？

translations.literal: Jing Province is not a place of strategic importance; its forces are few and weak; externally it is pressed by Liang raiders, internally it must resist Gao Huan's faction—this is a place where ruin is feared; how can it suffice to secure the great foundation?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province is not strategically vital; its forces are few and weak; externally it is harried by Liang raiders, internally it must resist Gao Huan's faction—there you would court ruin; how could that secure the dynasty?

sentences.zh: 以臣斷之，未見其可。

translations.literal: By my judgment, I do not see that it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment, I do not see how it can succeed."

sentences.zh: 」帝深納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor deeply accepted this.

sentences.zh: 及帝西遷，慶以母老不從。

translations.literal: When the Emperor moved west, Qing because his mother was old did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved west, Liu Qing did not follow because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信之鎮洛陽，乃得入關。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang, Qing was then able to enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang, Liu Qing was finally able to enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 除相府東閤祭酒，領記室，轉戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed eastern pavilion libationer in the chancellor's office, concurrently head of the secretariat, and was transferred to household-section staff member.
translations.idiomatic: He was made eastern pavilion libationer in the chancellor's office, concurrently head of the secretariat, and was transferred to the household section.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷大行臺郎中，領北華州長史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to director in the grand mobile office and concurrently chief administrator of Northern Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to director in the grand mobile office and concurrently chief administrator of Northern Hua.

sentences.zh: 十年，除尚書都兵，郎中如故，幷領記室。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed director of military affairs in the Masters of Writing; his directorship remained as before, and he also concurrently headed the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made director of military affairs in the Masters of Writing; he retained his directorship and also continued to head the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時北雍州獻白鹿，群臣欲草表陳賀。

translations.literal: At that time Northern Yong Province presented a white deer; the assembled ministers wished to draft a memorial of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Northern Yong presented a white deer; the ministers wished to draft a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 尚書蘇綽謂慶曰：「近代以來，文章華靡，逮于江左，彌復輕薄。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Su Chuo said to Qing: "In recent generations writing has grown ornate; reaching Jiangzuo it has become even more frivolous.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Su Chuo said to Liu Qing: "In recent times writing has grown ornate; in Jiangzuo it has become even more frivolous.

sentences.zh: 洛陽後進，祖述不已。

translations.literal: The later men of Luoyang imitate this without end.
translations.idiomatic: The younger writers of Luoyang imitate this without end.

sentences.zh: 相公柄民軌物，君職典文房，宜制此表，以革前弊。

translations.literal: The Chancellor holds the people to measure and governs things; your office oversees the scriptorium—you ought to compose this memorial to reform the earlier abuses."
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor governs the people and sets the standard; your office oversees the scriptorium—you should compose this memorial and reform the old abuses."

sentences.zh: 」慶操筆立成，辭兼文質。
