translations.literal: " Qing took up the brush and immediately finished it; the language combined literary polish with substance.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing took up the brush and finished it on the spot; the language combined polish with substance.

sentences.zh: 綽讀而笑曰：「枳橘猶自可移，況才子也。

translations.literal: Chuo read it and laughed, saying: "Even the bitter orange can change when transplanted—how much more a man of talent."
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo read it and laughed: "Even the bitter orange changes when transplanted—how much more a man of talent."

sentences.zh: 」尋以本官兼雍州別駕。

translations.literal: " Soon with his existing rank he was concurrently made vice-prefect of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon, retaining his existing rank, he was concurrently made vice-prefect of Yong.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王元欣，魏之懿親。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling Yuan Xin was a close kinsman of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangling Yuan Xin was a close kinsman of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 其甥孟氏，屢為匈橫。

translations.literal: His sister's son of the Meng clan repeatedly behaved with violence.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew of the Meng clan repeatedly behaved with violent arrogance.

sentences.zh: 或有告其盜牛。

translations.literal: Someone reported that he had stolen an ox.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that he had stolen an ox.

sentences.zh: 慶捕推得實，趣令就禁。

translations.literal: Qing arrested and investigated him, found the facts true, and hurriedly ordered him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing arrested and investigated him, found the charge true, and promptly ordered him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 孟氏殊無懼容，乃謂慶曰：「今若加以桎梏，後復何以脫之？

translations.literal: The Meng clan showed not the least fear, and said to Qing: "If you now put shackles on me, how later will you remove them?"
translations.idiomatic: Meng showed no fear at all and said to Liu Qing: "If you put shackles on me now, how will you remove them later?"

sentences.zh: 」欣亦遣使辨其無罪。

translations.literal: " Xin also sent an envoy to argue that he was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Xin also sent an envoy to argue that he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 孟氏由此益驕。

translations.literal: The Meng clan from this grew even more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: The Meng clan grew even more arrogant after this.

sentences.zh: 慶於是大集僚吏，盛言孟氏依倚權戚，侵虐之狀。

translations.literal: Qing thereupon greatly assembled the staff officials and fully described how the Meng clan relied on powerful kin and their acts of oppression and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing then assembled his staff and fully described how the Meng clan relied on powerful kin and oppressed the people.

sentences.zh: 言畢，便令笞殺之。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he immediately ordered him beaten to death with the whip.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, he immediately ordered Meng beaten to death with the whip.

sentences.zh: 此後貴戚斂手，不敢侵暴。

translations.literal: After this the noble kin restrained their hands and did not dare to oppress and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: After this the noble kin held back and dared not oppress the people.

sentences.zh: 有賈人持金二十斤，詣京師交易，寄人停止。

translations.literal: There was a merchant carrying twenty jin of gold who went to the capital to trade and lodged with a host.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant carrying twenty jin of gold went to the capital to trade and lodged with a host.

sentences.zh: 每欲出行，常自執管鑰。

translations.literal: Whenever he wished to go out, he always personally held the keys himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wished to go out, he always kept the keys on his person.

sentences.zh: 無何，緘閉不異而失之。

translations.literal: Before long, though the seal was unchanged, the gold was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, though the lock showed no sign of tampering, the gold was gone.

sentences.zh: 謂主人所竊，郡縣訊問，主人遂自誣服。

translations.literal: He thought the host had stolen it; the commandery and district interrogated him, and the host thereupon falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He thought the host had stolen it; the local authorities interrogated the host, who then falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 慶聞而歎之，乃召問賈人曰：「卿鑰恒置何處？

translations.literal: Qing heard of this and sighed; he thereupon summoned and questioned the merchant, saying: "Where do you always keep your keys?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing heard of this and sighed; he summoned the merchant and asked: "Where do you always keep your keys?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「恒自帶之。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I always carry them on my person."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "I always carry them on my person."

sentences.zh: 」慶曰：「頗與人同宿乎？

translations.literal: " Qing said: "Do you ever lodge with others?"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing asked: "Do you ever lodge with others?"

translations.literal: " He said: "No."
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "No."

sentences.zh: 」「與人同飲乎？

translations.literal: " "Do you ever drink with others?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Do you ever drink with others?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「日者曾與一沙門再度酣宴，醉而晝寢。

translations.literal: " He said: "The other day I twice drank heavily with a Buddhist monk; I was drunk and slept through the day."
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "The other day I twice drank heavily with a Buddhist monk; I was drunk and slept through the day."

sentences.zh: 」慶曰：「主人特以痛自誣，非盜也。

translations.literal: " Qing said: "The host only falsely confessed from pain; he is not the thief.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing said: "The host only confessed under torture; he is not the thief.

sentences.zh: 彼沙門乃真盜耳。

translations.literal: That monk is the real thief."
translations.idiomatic: That monk is the real thief."

sentences.zh: 」卽遣吏逮捕沙門，乃懷金逃匿。

translations.literal: " He immediately sent officials to arrest the monk; the monk had hidden the gold on his person and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately sent officials to arrest the monk, who had hidden the gold on his person and fled.

sentences.zh: 後捕得，盡獲所失之金。

translations.literal: Later he was captured, and all the lost gold was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He was later captured, and all the lost gold was recovered.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改三十六曹為十二部，詔以慶為計部郎中，別駕如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the thirty-six bureaus were changed to twelve departments; an edict made Qing director of the accounts department, his vice-prefectship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the thirty-six bureaus were reorganized into twelve departments; an edict made Liu Qing director of the accounts department while retaining his vice-prefectship.

sentences.zh: 有胡家被劫，郡縣按察，莫知賊所，鄰近被囚繫者甚多。

translations.literal: There was a Hu household that had been robbed; the commandery and district investigated, but none knew where the bandits were; many of the neighbors were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: A Hu household was robbed; the local authorities investigated but could not find the bandits, and many neighbors were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 慶以賊徒旣衆，似是烏合，旣非舊交，必相疑阻，可以詐求之。

translations.literal: Qing thought that since the bandits were numerous, they seemed to be a mob gathered together; since they were not old associates, they must suspect and obstruct one another—one could seek them by deception.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing reasoned that since the bandits were numerous they must be a mob of strangers who would suspect and distrust one another—and that they could therefore be found by a ruse.

sentences.zh: 乃作匿名書多牓官門曰：「我等共劫胡家，徒侶混雜，終恐洩露。

translations.literal: Thereupon anonymous letters were made and many placards posted at government gates, saying: "We together robbed a Hu household; our companions are mixed, and in the end we fear exposure.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous letters were then posted at many government gates, saying: "We robbed a Hu household together; our band is mixed, and we fear exposure in the end.

sentences.zh: 今欲首，懼不免誅。

translations.literal: Now we wish to surrender first, but fear we cannot escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to turn ourselves in, but fear we cannot escape execution.

sentences.zh: 若聽先首免罪，便欲來告。

translations.literal: If we are allowed to surrender first and be exempt from punishment, we will come and report.
translations.idiomatic: If those who surrender first are spared punishment, we will come forward.

sentences.zh: 」慶乃復施免罪之牓。

translations.literal: " Qing thereupon again posted placards granting exemption from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing then posted placards again offering amnesty.

sentences.zh: 居二日，廣

translations.literal: After two days, Guang
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, Guang

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yang]

sentences.zh: 〔陵〕王欣家奴面縛自告牓下。

translations.literal: [Ling] Prince Xin's household slave, bound and facing forward, surrendered himself beneath the placard.
translations.idiomatic: [Ling] A bound household slave of Prince Xin of Guangling surrendered beneath the placard.

sentences.zh: 因此推窮，盡獲黨與。

translations.literal: Through this the case was pursued to the end, and all accomplices were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation ran its course from this, and every accomplice was captured.

sentences.zh: 慶之守正明察，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Qing's uprightness in holding to principle and clear discernment were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing's integrity and sharp discernment were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 每歎曰：「昔于公斷獄無私，闢高門可以待封。

translations.literal: He often sighed and said: "In olden days Lord Yu judged cases without partiality, and built a high gate awaiting enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed and said: "In olden days Lord Yu judged cases without partiality and built a high gate awaiting enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 儻斯言有驗，吾其庶幾乎。

translations.literal: If that saying proves true, I may come close to it.
translations.idiomatic: If that saying proves true, I may come close to it."

sentences.zh: 」十三年，封清河縣男，邑二百戶，兼尚書右丞，攝計部。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was enfeoffed Baron of Qinghe county, fief two hundred households, and concurrently made right vice director of the Masters of Writing, acting head of the accounts section.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was enfeoffed Baron of Qinghe with two hundred households, made concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and put in charge of the accounts section.

sentences.zh: 十四年，正右丞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was made regular right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became regular right vice director.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗怒安定國臣王茂，將殺之，而非其罪。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once in anger targeted Wang Mao, a subject of the state of Ding'an, and was about to kill him, though the crime was not his.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once in anger moved against Wang Mao, a Ding'an subject, and was about to execute him though he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 朝臣咸知，而莫敢諫。

translations.literal: The court ministers all knew it, yet none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Every court minister knew it, yet none dared remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 慶乃進曰：「王茂無罪，奈何殺之？

translations.literal: Qing then advanced and said: "Wang Mao is without guilt—why kill him?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing then stepped forward and said: "Wang Mao is innocent—why kill him?

sentences.zh: 」太祖愈怒，聲色甚厲，謂慶曰：「王茂當死，卿若明其無罪，亦須坐之。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor grew still angrier; his voice and bearing were very stern, and he said to Qing: "Wang Mao ought to die; if you make clear he is without guilt, you too must share the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai grew angrier still; his voice and bearing turned harsh, and he told Liu Qing: "Wang Mao deserves death. If you insist he is innocent, you too must share the punishment.

sentences.zh: 」乃執慶於前。

translations.literal: " He thereupon seized Qing before him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Liu Qing seized before him.

sentences.zh: 慶辭氣不撓，抗聲曰：「竊聞君有不達者為不明，臣有不爭者為不忠。

translations.literal: Qing's tone and spirit did not bend; he raised his voice and said: "I have heard that a lord who does not penetrate matters is not enlightened, and a minister who does not contend is not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing's tone did not waver; he answered boldly: "I have heard that a ruler who fails to see clearly is unenlightened, and a minister who will not contend is disloyal.

sentences.zh: 慶謹竭愚誠，實不敢愛死，但懼公為不明之君耳。

translations.literal: Qing respectfully exhausts his foolish sincerity and truly dares not spare death, but only fears that my lord will be an unenlightened ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing offers his utmost honest counsel and truly does not cling to life, but only fears that you will prove an unenlightened ruler.

sentences.zh: 願深察之。

translations.literal: I wish you would examine this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to look into this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃悟而赦茂，已不及矣。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor thereupon understood and pardoned Mao, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then understood and pardoned Wang Mao, but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 太祖默然。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai fell silent.

sentences.zh: 明日，謂慶曰：「吾不用卿言，遂令王茂冤死。

translations.literal: The next day, he said to Qing: "I did not use your words, and so caused Wang Mao to die unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told Liu Qing: "I did not heed you, and so let Wang Mao die unjustly.

sentences.zh: 可賜茂家錢帛，以旌吾過。

translations.literal: You may grant Mao's household money and silk to mark my fault.
translations.idiomatic: Grant Wang Mao's household money and silk to mark my fault.

sentences.zh: 」尋進爵為子，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: " Soon he was advanced in nobility to viscount, and his fief was increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qing was soon raised to viscount, and his fief was increased by three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加平南將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was given the added title general who pacifies the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was given the added title general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 十六年，太祖東討，以慶為大行臺右丞，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Grand Progenitor campaigned east; Qing was made right vice director of the great mobile secretariat and given the added title general who comforts the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai campaigned east, Liu Qing was made right vice director of the great mobile secretariat and given the added title general who comforts the army.

sentences.zh: 還轉尚書右丞，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On returning he was transferred to right vice director of the Masters of Writing and given the added title attendant-in-ordinary of direct liaison.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to right vice director of the Masters of Writing and given the added title attendant-in-ordinary of direct liaison.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，除民部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Fei of Wei, he was appointed minister of the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Western Wei Emperor Fei's reign, he was appointed minister of the people.

sentences.zh: 慶威儀端肅，樞機明辨。

translations.literal: Qing's bearing and ritual were dignified and solemn; in the pivot of affairs he was clear and discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing's bearing was dignified and solemn, and in affairs of state he was clear and discerning.

sentences.zh: 太祖每發號令，常使慶宣之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Grand Progenitor issued orders, he always had Qing proclaim them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai issued orders, he always had Liu Qing proclaim them.

sentences.zh: 天性抗直，無所回避。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and outspoken, yielding to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and outspoken by nature, he yielded to nothing.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦以此深委仗焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor also for this reason deeply entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also for this reason placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 二年，授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-to-three-division commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-to-three-division commander.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝初，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射，轉左僕射，領著作。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was advanced to grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander, and right vice premier; he was transferred to left vice premier and concurrently directed the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Western Wei Emperor Gong's reign, he was raised to grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander, and right vice premier; he was transferred to left vice premier and put in charge of the Bureau of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜司會中大夫。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed director of accounts, grand master.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed director of accounts, grand master.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，賜姓宇文氏，進爵平齊縣公，增邑通前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was granted the surname Yuwen, advanced in nobility to Duke of Pingqi county, and his fief was increased together with the former to one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was granted the surname Yuwen, raised to Duke of Pingqi, and his fief was increased together with the former to one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 晉公護初攝政，欲引為腹心。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Hu first held the regency, he wished to draw him in as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu first held the regency, he wished to draw Liu Qing in as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 慶辭之，頗忤旨。

translations.literal: Qing declined, greatly going against the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing declined, greatly going against Hu's intent.

sentences.zh: 又與楊寬有隙，及寬參知政事，慶遂見疏忌，出為萬州刺史。

translations.literal: He also had a rift with Yang Kuan; when Kuan joined in directing government affairs, Qing thereupon met with estrangement and suspicion and was sent out as inspector of Wan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a rift with Yang Kuan; when Kuan joined in directing government affairs, Liu Qing met with estrangement and suspicion and was sent out as inspector of Wan Province.

sentences.zh: 世宗尋悟，留為雍州別駕，領京兆尹。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong soon understood, kept him as vice governor of Yong Province, and concurrently made him metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong soon saw his error, kept Liu Qing as vice governor of Yong Province, and concurrently made him metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，除宜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, he was appointed inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng 2 he was appointed inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 慶自為郎，迄于司會，府庫倉儲，竝其職也。

translations.literal: From the time Qing served as a gentleman of the palace until he reached director of accounts, treasury stores and granaries were all within his duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Liu Qing served as a palace gentleman until he became director of accounts, treasury stores and granaries had all been within his duties.

sentences.zh: 及在宜州，寬為小冢宰，乃囚慶故吏，求其罪失。

translations.literal: When he was at Yi Province, Kuan served as minor chief minister; he then imprisoned Qing's former subordinates and sought their faults and lapses.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Qing was at Yi Province, Yang Kuan served as minor chief minister; Kuan then imprisoned Liu Qing's former subordinates and searched for faults and lapses.

sentences.zh: 按驗積六十餘日，吏或有死於獄者，終無所言，唯得剩錦數匹。

translations.literal: The investigation continued for more than sixty days; some subordinates died in prison, yet in the end none spoke, and only a few bolts of surplus brocade were found.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation ran for more than sixty days; some subordinates died in prison, yet in the end none confessed, and only a few bolts of surplus brocade were found.

sentences.zh: 時人服其廉慎。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his integrity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired his integrity and caution.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，又入為司會。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he again entered court as director of accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 3 he again entered court as director of accounts.

sentences.zh: 機字匡時，少有令譽，風儀辭令，為當世所推。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Kuangshi, from youth had a fine reputation; his bearing, speech, and commands were praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Kuangshi, had a fine reputation from youth; his bearing, speech, and command of language were praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 曆小納言、開府儀同三司、司宗中大夫。

translations.literal: He served as junior remonstrator, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander, and director of the clan, grand master.
translations.idiomatic: He served as junior remonstrator, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander, and director of the clan, grand master.

sentences.zh: 大象中，御正上大夫、華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, he was director of censors, upper grand master, and inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he was director of censors, upper grand master, and inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 機弟弘，字匡道，少聰穎，亦善草隸，博涉群書，辭彩雅贍。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Hong, styled Kuangdao, from youth was clever and quick; he also excelled at cursive and clerical script, broadly read many books, and his literary color was elegant and rich.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Hong, styled Kuangdao, was clever and quick from youth; he also excelled at cursive and clerical script, read widely, and wrote with elegant richness.

sentences.zh: 與弘農楊素為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: With Yang Su of Hongnong he formed a friendship of utmost trust.
translations.idiomatic: With Yang Su of Hongnong he formed a friendship of utmost trust.

sentences.zh: 解巾中外府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He first took office as recorder in the central and exterior headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: He first took office as recorder in the central and exterior headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 建德初，除內史上士，歷小宮尹、御正上士。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiande, he was appointed upper master of the secretariat; he served as junior palace steward and upper master of the directorate of censors.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiande he was appointed upper master of the secretariat; he served as junior palace steward and upper master of the directorate of censors.

translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Wang Yanmin on a friendly mission; Emperor Gaozu ordered Hong to host him.

sentences.zh: 偃民謂弘曰：「來日，至於藍田，正逢滋水暴長，所齎國信，溺而從流。

translations.idiomatic: Yanmin told Hong: "The other day, when we reached Lantian, the Zi River suddenly flooded; the state letter we carried was drowned and swept away.

sentences.zh: 今所進者，假之從吏。

translations.literal: What we present now was borrowed from attendant clerks.
translations.idiomatic: What we present now was borrowed from attendant clerks.

sentences.zh: 請勒下流人，見為追尋此物也。

translations.idiomatic: Please order people downstream to look out and recover it for us.

translations.idiomatic: " Hong said: "In olden days Chunyu's presenting an empty cage was praised in the histories as admirable.

sentences.zh: 足下假物而進，詎是陳君之命乎。

translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned, he was appointed director of the secretariat, upper master, and transferred to lower grand master of the directorate of censors.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于官，時年三十一。

translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office, aged thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚惜之。

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu deeply regretted his loss.

translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Jin Province.

translations.idiomatic: Yang Su composed a dirge for him, saying: "Wang Bi of Shanyang—his elegance has passed forever.

translations.idiomatic: Xun Can of Yingchuan—fallen without season.

translations.idiomatic: A collected works of his circulated in the world.

translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing had three elder brothers—Zhuo, Qiu, and Gui; Qiu and Gui each have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 鷟好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhuo loved learning and was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo loved learning and was skilled at composing prose.

translations.literal: He was recorder in the staff of Prince of Linhuai of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was recorder on the staff of the Prince of Linhuai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

translations.literal: His son Daiwei, styled Xiaosun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daiwei, styled Xiaosun.

sentences.zh: 深沉有度量，少好學。

translations.literal: Deep and reserved, with breadth of mind, from youth he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and reserved, with breadth of mind, he loved learning from youth.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺三寸，美風儀，善占對。

translations.literal: His height was eight feet three inches; he had fine bearing and was skilled at ready replies.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet three inches tall, had fine bearing, and was skilled at ready replies.

sentences.zh: 韓賢素為洛州刺史，召為主簿。

translations.literal: Han Xian had long been inspector of Luo Province and summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian, long inspector of Luo Province, summoned him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後與諸父歸朝，太祖辟為參軍。

translations.literal: Later he returned to court with his uncles; the Grand Progenitor recruited him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to court with his uncles; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai recruited him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 時侯景作亂江右，太祖令帶韋使江、郢二州，與梁邵陵、南平二王通好。

translations.literal: At the time Hou Jing was in rebellion in the lands south of the Yangtze; the Grand Progenitor ordered Daiwei to go as envoy to Jiang and Ying provinces and open friendly relations with the Liang princes of Shaoling and Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hou Jing was in rebellion south of the Yangtze; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Daiwei to go as envoy to Jiang and Ying provinces and open friendly relations with the Liang princes of Shaoling and Nanping.

sentences.zh: 行至安州，值假寶等反，帶韋乃矯為太祖書以撫安之，竝卽降附。

translations.literal: When he reached An Province, he encountered the rebellion of Jiabao and others; Daiwei thereupon forged a letter in the Grand Progenitor's name to reassure and pacify them, and they all at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached An Province, Jiabao and others had risen in rebellion; Daiwei forged a letter in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's name to reassure them, and they submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 旣至郢，見邵陵，具申太祖意。

translations.literal: When he reached Ying, he saw the Prince of Shaoling and fully explained the Grand Progenitor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Ying, he saw the Prince of Shaoling and fully explained Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's intent.

translations.literal: The Prince of Shaoling thereupon
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shaoling thereupon

translations.idiomatic: [variant: shi]

translations.literal: sent an envoy to follow Daiwei back with the reply.
translations.idiomatic: sent an envoy to follow Daiwei back with the reply.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，授轉輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Because the mission accorded with intent, he was appointed and transferred to auxiliary state general and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mission accorded with intent, he was appointed auxiliary state general and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 十七年，太祖遣大將軍達奚武經略漢川，以帶韋為治行臺左丞，從軍南討。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Grand Progenitor dispatched grand general Daxi Wu to operate in Hanzhong; Daiwei was made left vice director of the governing mobile secretariat and followed the army south in the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai dispatched grand general Daxi Wu to operate in Hanzhong; Daiwei was made left vice director of the governing mobile secretariat and followed the army south.

sentences.zh: 時梁宜豐侯蕭循守南鄭，武攻之未拔。

translations.literal: At the time the Liang Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xun, held Nanzheng; Wu attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Liang Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xun, held Nanzheng; Daxi Wu attacked but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 乃令帶韋入城說循曰：「足下所固者險，所恃者援，所守者民。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Daiwei to enter the city and persuade Xun, saying: "What you rely on is terrain, what you depend on is reinforcements, and what you hold is the people.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Daiwei to enter the city and persuade Xiao Xun, saying: "What you rely on is terrain, what you depend on is reinforcements, and what you hold is the people.

sentences.zh: 今王師深入棧道，長驅漢川，此則所憑之險不足固也；

translations.literal: Now the royal army has penetrated deep along the plank road and drives straight through Hanzhong—then the terrain you rely on is not enough to hold;
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal army has penetrated deep along the plank road and drives straight through Hanzhong—then the terrain you rely on is not enough to hold;

sentences.zh: 武興陷沒於前，白馬破亡於後，自餘川谷酋豪，路阻而不敢進，此則所望之援不可恃也；

translations.literal: Wuxing has fallen in front and Baima has been destroyed behind; the remaining chieftains of valleys and streams, blocked on the road, dare not advance—then the reinforcements you look to cannot be depended on;
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing has fallen in front and Baima has been destroyed behind; the remaining chieftains of valleys and streams, blocked on the road, dare not advance—then the reinforcements you look to cannot be depended on;

sentences.zh: 夫顧親戚，懼誅夷，貪榮慕利，此生人常也，今大兵總至，長圍四合，戮逃亡以勸安居，賞先降以招後服，人人懷轉禍之計，家家圖安堵之謀，此則所部之民不可守也。

translations.literal: to care for kin, fear execution and extermination, covet glory and prize profit—this is the constant of living men; now the great army has all arrived, the long encirclement closes on four sides, punishing flight to encourage those who stay at peace, rewarding those who surrender first to win those who come later—every man harbors a plan to turn calamity aside, every household plots for settled security—then the people under your command cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: To care for kin, fear execution, covet glory and prize profit—this is human nature; now the great army has arrived, the long encirclement closes on four sides, punishing flight to encourage those who stay, rewarding those who surrender first to win those who come later—every man plots to turn calamity aside, every household seeks settled security—then the people under your command cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 且足下本朝喪亂，社稷無主，盡忠將何所托，死節不足成名，竊為足下不取也。

translations.literal: Moreover your own court is in disorder and the altars of soil and grain have no lord; to whom would complete loyalty be entrusted, and dying for principle would not suffice to make a name—I privately consider this unworthy of you.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your own court is in disorder and the altars of soil and grain have no lord; to whom would complete loyalty be entrusted, and dying for principle would not suffice to make a name—I privately consider this unworthy of you.

sentences.zh: 僕聞賢者相時而動，智者因變立功。

translations.literal: I have heard that the worthy move according to the times, and the wise achieve merit by adapting to change.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the worthy move according to the times, and the wise achieve merit by adapting to change.

sentences.zh: 當今為足下計者，莫若肉袒軍門，歸命下吏，免生民于塗炭，全髮膚於孝道。

translations.literal: For what is planned for Your Excellency now, nothing surpasses baring the shoulder at the army gate, submitting to the lower officials, sparing the people from charred bones, and preserving hair and skin in filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: The best course I can urge for you now is to come to the camp gate with bared shoulder, surrender to the officials, spare your people the torments of war, and preserve your own life in filial duty.

sentences.zh: 必當紆青拖紫，裂土分珪，名重當時，業光後嗣。

translations.literal: You will surely be granted green sash and purple robe, lands split and jade tablets distributed, name heavy in the age, achievement shining on posterity.
translations.idiomatic: You will surely receive high office and enfeoffment, win weighty fame in your own day, and leave glory to your descendants.

translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, he was rewarded with upper opening-office equal-in-protocol grand general, raised to duke, and given one thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 〔亡〕革慮；

translations.literal: [fall] alter resolve;
translations.idiomatic: fall of dynasties alter their resolve;

sentences.zh: 崎嶇危難，不以夷險易心。

translations.literal: through rugged peril, they did not let ease or hardship change their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: through rugged peril they did not let ease or hardship change their hearts.

sentences.zh: 斯固篤終之士。

translations.literal: These were indeed men who saw things through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: These were men who truly saw things through to the end.

sentences.zh: 柳慶束帶立朝，懷匪躬之節；

translations.literal: Liu Qing girded his belt and stood at court, harboring the integrity of giving body to the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing girded himself and stood at court with the self-sacrificing integrity of a true minister;

sentences.zh: 蒞官從政，著清白之美。

translations.literal: holding office and administering government, he displayed the beauty of pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In office and in governance he displayed unstained integrity.

sentences.zh: 竝遭逢興運，各展志能，譽重搢紳，望隆端揆，非虛云也。

translations.literal: Both encountered a rising fortune, each displayed ambition and ability, reputation weighty among gentry-officials, esteem lofty as chief ministers—not empty praise.
translations.idiomatic: Both rode a rising age, each put his gifts to full use, won weighty repute among the gentry, and stood as figures fit for the highest office—that praise was no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 然慶畏避權寵，違忤宰臣，雖取詘於一時，實獲申於千載矣。

translations.literal: Yet Qing feared and avoided power and favor, went against the chief minister; though he suffered setback for a time, in truth he won vindication for a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Qing shunned power and favor and defied the chief minister; though he lost ground for a time, he won vindication for a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
